newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-GUSTAFSSON EYES DAVIS CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GUSTAFSSON EYES DAVIS CUP FINAL.

text.p: Magnus Gustafsson is dreaming of a return to Sweden's Davis Cup team which hosts the final against France at the end of the month.
"I had not thought about being selected until now that I'm playing like this," said Gustafsson, who on Friday reached the semifinals of the Paris Open after beating Swiss Marc Rosset 6-2 3-6 6-2.
But Gustafsson said he did not expect to displace automatically either Stefan Edberg or Thomas Enqvist, one of whom he will meet in Saturday's semifinals at Bercy.
"They are both playing good tennis too, it would be different otherwise," said the 28th ranked Swede who has a 7-2 record in Davis Cup singles.
"But I think that I could get in if they name five in the team and then decide who plays after the practices."
Gustafsson, whose highest world ranking was 10 in 1991, has also eliminated ninth seed Andre Agassi and eighth seed Wayne Ferreira in the Paris Open.
The 29-year-old said it was his dream as a child to play for Sweden in the Davis Cup.
"I was so nervous the first time, but I love it. I'm never so nervous when I'm playing for myself."
He is recovering his status in the game after a year out with shoulder problems that included surgery. He was ranked 611 when he came back in May 1995.
He has won two singles titles this year and has seven altogether.
"The Davis Cup is very big in Sweden. Swedes mostly practise team sports, like soccer and ice hockey," he said.
"Tennis has dipped a bit in Sweden since the six Davis Cup victories, but it's coming back."
Gustafsson said Bjorn Borg and organised club tennis in Sweden were behind his country's success in the Davis Cup.
"A lot of people get the possibility to play tennis because it's not so expensive as in other countries. I competed with 240 kids of my age in junior championships, all trying to be the best.
"In Sweden, to be the best you also have to be one of the best in the world."
